origin: Original workshop built by Muse (AI assistant) on 20 November 2026 at Steven Powell's direction, from the wave-2 candidate list in the Everyday Cool ideas side chat that morning: he picked Sound, Time, and Light from the list (placing knots in the Survival Guide and flight in Physics himself), set the build order — Sound first, Time second, Light third — and while Sound was being built gave Light its design note in the same breath as Sound's music wing: Sound gets music theory because music is math geometry with sound, and 'same for light really with it's cord' — light gets colour theory and its colour chords, with a cross-link to Math the same way. The room carries twin mixing benches (three lamps summing channel by channel to white, red over green making yellow; and the printer's cyan, magenta, and yellow as multiplying reflectance profiles whose built-in leak lands the full mixture at a warm near-black, about rgb(10, 8, 8) — the bench's explanation for the K in CMYK), a twelve-hue colour wheel striking chords by angle (complementary 180°, triadic 120° steps, analogous neighbours, split-complementary flanks) presented as the twin of Everyday Sound's circle of fifths, a thin-lens ray bench (1/f = 1/do + 1/di; f = 10 cm and an object at 30 cm giving an inverted image at 15 cm, magnification −0.5; a magnifying-glass virtual image inside the focal length), a Rayleigh scattering bench (blue 450 nm scattered (650/450)^4 ≈ 4.35 times red 650 nm; air mass driving the sun from near-white to deep red while the sky takes the scattered blue), a shadows-through-the-day bench on a compass rose (solar altitude and azimuth from latitude, declination, and hour angle; at equinox noon at 41.3°N a stick's shadow is its height × tan(41.3°)), and a spectrum slider (380–750 nm, frequencies from f = c/λ at the exact modern c, infrared and ultraviolet labelled rather than painted because they have no colour for us). The banner shows a friendly robot holding a glass prism up into a sunbeam, the spectrum fanning across the workbench, and a twelve-hue colour wheel leaning against the bench nearby. It enters the catalog under 'Science,' immediately after Everyday Time, as the thirteenth door of The STEM Room. This folder is the maintained original.
